This is a nonfatal sign-label ambiguity, not an erroneous count or a use of controlled sign equivalence. The original citation supplies a unique phase in [0,2π), whereas the theorem identifies it as lying in (−π,π) and calls a procedure admitting only [0,2π) inputs. At a=3/4 and φ=2π/3 the matching tangent is −√3/2, so the supplier phase exceeds π. Without the missing lift the dependency interface cannot be applied as stated. Repaired by defining the signed representative from the canonical matched phase and canonically lifting both signed phase labels at every algorithm call; periodicity is proved in step 1.1. The guarantees and full parameter range are preserved.
